newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: AGENCY TO BOOST INVESTMENTS PLANNED.
newsitem.headline: AGENCY TO BOOST INVESTMENTS PLANNED.

text.p: Lithuania's European Affairs ministry said on Wednesday it wanted to found an economic development agency to stimulate foreign investment.

"The cabinet will discuss the merger of Lithuania's investment and export development agencies into an economic development agency," deputy minister for European affairs Mindaugas Paunksnis told Reuters.
"The new agency will operate under the supervision of our ministry and its main task will be to encourage foreign investments into the country," Paunksnis added.
Lithuania is considered as a laggard behind its Baltic neighbours Latvia and Estonia in foreign investments which amounted to just $450 million at the end of 1996.
The ministry expects the new agency to provide better information to foreign investors and to work actively in local market research and marketing.
"If the decision is approved in the cabinet meeting today we hope it will start operating in a month or two," Paunksnis said.

The right-wing government which swept to power in late 1996 has acted to change the investment climate in the country and has unveiled plans to privatise 14 key companies in the energy, transport and communications sectors to attract investors.
